title: Raman Circular Dichroism Reveals Higher-Order Quantum Geometry of Magnons
authors: Yong Chan Kim, Youngsu Choi, Kwang-Yong Choi, Kyusung Hwang
abstract: We develop a gauge-invariant theory of higher-order magnon quantum geometry probed by two-magnon Raman circular dichroism (RCD). The Raman operator decomposes into Berry connections, covariant derivatives, and products of Berry connections, giving rise to quantum geometric tensors beyond the quantum metric and Berry curvature. Applying this theory to a field-polarized Kitaev magnet, we show that higher-order geometric tensors govern the dichroic response. Our results establish RCD as a spectroscopic probe of generalized magnon quantum geometry.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to characterize the higher-order quantum geometry of magnons in magnetic materials using two-magnon Raman Circular Dichroism (RCD). By decomposing the RCD signal into six distinct geometric tensor contributions, the authors establish RCD as a powerful, non-trivial spectroscopic tool for probing generalized quantum geometry beyond standard metrics.
main_problem: Developing a gauge-invariant theory to probe the higher-order quantum geometry of magnons using two-magnon Raman Circular Dichroism (RCD).
main_result: RCD is established as a spectroscopic probe for generalized magnon quantum geometry, with the spectrum being governed by higher-order geometric tensors.
method: The theory decomposes the Raman operator into Berry connections and covariant derivatives, leading to the identification of six distinct higher-order quantum-geometric tensors that contribute to the two-magnon RCD intensity.
model_or_system: The study applies the theory to a field-polarized Kitaev magnet, modeled by a spin Hamiltonian, and analyzes magnon excitations using Linear Spin-Wave Theory (LSWT).
key_observables: Two-magnon RCD intensity, $I_{2M}^{RCD}(\omega)$, and six higher-order quantum-geometric tensors (QGTs).
important_parameters: Kitaev coupling constant ($K$), exchange coupling ($J$), applied magnetic field ($h$), and field angle ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on LSWT and the successful decomposition of the Raman operator into specific geometric terms using projector representations.
figures_summary: Figures show the RCD intensity dependence on the magnetic field angle, resolved into three two-magnon sectors, and decomposed into six distinct geometric components.
paper_structure: The paper systematically builds the theory by defining single-state quantum geometric tensors, deriving their projector representations for second-order terms, and finally applying this framework to calculate the two-magnon RCD intensity as a sum of six geometric contributions.
why_interesting: The work provides a rigorous theoretical framework connecting measurable spectroscopic signals (RCD) directly to abstract, higher-order geometric properties of the underlying quantum excitations (magnons).
